record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; linked files and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports behavioral results for public, weight-edited abliterated checkpoints, testing practical refusal removal and cross-language effects with a different intervention from the original residual-stream ablation.
record.gate_note: The README reports compliance rates for base and abliterated checkpoints by model size and language, plus aggregate rates and mechanistic summaries. The README does not report an addition intervention, a general-capability evaluation, or outcomes for harmless prompts. Its listed harmless prompts and scripts do not themselves report results.
record.test_reason: It runs harmful prompts in 7 languages through base and public abliterated Gemma 4 checkpoints (E2B, E4B, 31B) and reports judged compliance. This bears on V2 (weight-edit removal in released models) and V6 (transfer across languages) in a new model family and size range. It is not a stated replication of the original recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also say they extend Wang et al. to sub-7B Gemma 4. They report that removing the English direction collapses safety across all 7 languages, and that the low-resource-is-more-vulnerable prediction is refuted, with Hindi the most consistently safe. They add that the compliance peak and the cross-lingual cosine peak coincide at E4B, and that base compliance rises monotonically with size.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates public Huihui-ai weight-edited checkpoints rather than directly applying the original residual-stream projection and addition interventions. This is a tool/research repository, not a stated replication of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported compliance varies across model size and language; the README reports the largest mean change at E4B and different highest-compliance languages across sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Silhouette scores of harmful/harmless clustering decrease with size (0.29, 0.26, 0.23). The calculation and its link to refusal mediation are not stated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separability of harmful vs harmless activations decreases with model size in Gemma 4 Dense.

record.problems: The README reports no uncertainty intervals or statistical tests. It relies on Claude Haiku 4.5 judging 100 prompts per language cell and reports no general-capability outcomes. The linked data and analysis files were not available for inspection in this record.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported README results bearing on the tested versions were omitted. The README's aggregate and per-language compliance results and the stated mechanistic summaries are recorded.

untested.parts: No activation ablation or addition of the direction, no induced refusal on harmless prompts, and no capability check.
No general-capability or harmless-prompt evaluation of the edited checkpoints. The weight-edit details (layer, prompt set) are not reported.
No base-to-instruct transfer, no transfer across model variants or families, and no other languages.

missing.what: Per-language-pair cosine similarities between refusal directions, which are needed to judge whether a mean of about 0.3 indicates a shared direction.
Per-language silhouette scores and PCA plots.
Whether huihui-ai computed the direction from English-only prompts. The README asserts this but does not document it, and the V6 reading depends on it.

record.verdict_notes: The source is a README only, with no uncertainty estimates, and the 4-bit quantization could affect the results. The non-English rows keep V2 and V6 links: they are partial for V2 (incomplete removal) but show transfer that matches English for V6. The cosine rows stay cannot_determine because no reference level is given. The record's V6 limits_scope label was dropped because its reason (incomplete compliance) concerns V2, not transfer.

versions.untested_parts: No reported direct projection of the difference-in-means direction out of every layer and position; no addition intervention inducing refusal on harmless requests; no general-capability check.
Does not report the weight-edit procedure or its effect on general capabilities in detail; evaluates public Huihui-ai abliterated checkpoints.
No jailbreak or training-against-ablation experiment is reported.
The README reports cosine and silhouette summaries but does not report a test comparing single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
Tests three Dense Gemma 4 instruct sizes and seven languages; does not test other model families, base-to-instruct transfer, or languages outside those listed.
No comparison of refusal-training methods, data, or training stages is reported.

source_check.notes: The text is the README only (titled 'Preliminary Results'). It gives no judge prompt, no CIs, a single greedy run, both models 4-bit NF4, prompts translated by Claude, and no capability measure. The README's mechanistic result (mean cross-lingual refusal-direction cosine 0.31 E2B / 0.37 E4B / 0.27 31B; silhouette 0.29 -> 0.26 -> 0.23) bears on V6 and should be recorded as rows if absent. The authors' headline is a non-monotonic size curve peaking at E4B, with E2B the least compromised. That runs against their own smaller-is-more-vulnerable hypothesis.

statements.correction: gh:gustipardo: huihui-ai abliterated Gemma 4, mean judged compliance across 7 languages: E2B 4.1% -> 42.9% (+38.8 pp), E4B 10.7% -> 68.1% (+57.4 pp), 31B 13.1% -> 64.4% (+51.3 pp). That is partial removal (limits_scope for V2), not challenges. Belongs under limits_scope / partial removal.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but listing this study as 'challenges' (refusal kept) misreads it. The edit raises compliance by 38.8 to 57.4 pp at every size, so the effect is partial, not absent. The authors call E4B removal 'nearly complete'. The measure is judged compliance, not a refusal rate.

None for this study. The README describes the edit as English-direction abliteration. It does not document huihui-ai's prompt set. Decoding is greedy only (seed 42), so seed/temperature variation is untested here too.

statements.correction: gh:gustipardo E2B: ES 7% -> 47% (+40 pp), HI 2% -> 39% (+37 pp), EN 4% -> 42% (+38 pp). Abliterated compliance across all 7 languages at E2B is 39-47%. HI is lowest at every size (39/65/60) but within about 10 pp of the others. No CIs, n=100 per cell.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but they are the max and min E2B languages. The gains are almost the same (ES +40 pp vs HI +37 pp; EN +38 pp). That is weak evidence that evaluation language changes the edit's effect. n=100 per cell, no uncertainty reported.
